articles.title: US Open 2026: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz return in mixed doubles
articles.summary: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz were among the star double-acts in New York as the US Open mixed doubles competition got under way on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Enjoy it - and do what Serena Williams tells you to.

That was how Carlos Alcaraz settled back into competitive action at the US Open, partnering the American great as she returned to her home slam after a four-year absence.

The tournament's revamped mixed doubles format has attracted criticism for favouring the allure of the sport's top singles stars at the expense of established doubles players.

But the crowds turned out and produced a terrific atmosphere for the tournament's headline act, with about 15,000 people packed inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.

All four doubles specialist pairings lost to a team of singles players on Tuesday, while Alcaraz and Williams fell in the quarter-finals.

Seven-time major winner Alcaraz was playing his first competitive match since April after injuring his wrist, while 23-time Grand Slam champion Williams was competing in New York for the first time since she "evolved away" from tennis in 2022.

The pair were greeted by huge cheers and were roared on throughout their opening 5-3 4-1 win against Great Britain's Lloyd Glasspool and New Zealand's Erin Routliffe.

The 44-year-old Williams won the US Open mixed doubles title in its original format alongside Max Mirnyi in 1998 - five years before Alcaraz was born.

Almost 30 years later, Williams still had the competitive desire. She and Alcaraz enjoyed the occasion, playing with smiles on their faces and roaring each other on after winning a point.

Interviewed during a change of ends, Alcaraz said: "I'm playing next to the one and only Serena Williams, so what else can I do? Just enjoy and try to do the things she told me to do."

Their partnership improved rapidly in their first match as they won eight of the final nine games to seal victory.

However, they were denied a place in Wednesday's semi-finals by Italy's world number six Flavio Cobolli and Swiss team-mate Belinda Bencic, who won 5-4 (7-4) 4-1.

Wawrinka 'grateful' despite no US Open wildcard Published 10 hours ago

Wawrinka 'grateful' despite no US Open wildcard

Returning Alcaraz 'almost forgot how this feels'

While Williams will not contest the singles at the US Open - she has not competed in that format since injuring her knee at Wimbledon - Tuesday's matches provided the returning Alcaraz with valuable court time.

The Spaniard admitted he felt nervous before stepping out on the court - in part due to partnering six-time US Open women's singles champion Williams.

"I think everyone could see I was really nervous, I double-faulted on the first point," Alcaraz said after their opening win.

"I was out for almost five months and I almost forgot how it feels stepping out on the court once again.

"It [took] just a couple of games [to settle] and she made it very easy for me to enjoy it and try to go for it."

For Williams, a return to the Arthur Ashe Stadium was something she did not believe would come around again.

"It's always amazing to be here. I never expected to be back on this court," Williams said.

"It was just a really cool moment. I never thought this would happen."

The controversial revamped mixed doubles format, introduced last year, pits established doubles players against some of the sport's biggest singles stars.

The tournament takes place the week before the singles draw gets under way and allows direct entry into the main draw for top-ranked singles players and wildcards.

Established doubles players such as Britons Glasspool and Henry Patten had to come through two qualifying rounds on Monday.

Top-ranked players Patten and Katerina Siniakova advanced to the quarter-finals before losing to husband-and-wife duo Gael Monfils and Elina Svitolina.

Discussing their dynamic, with a semi-final against Cobolli and Bencic to come, Frenchman Monfils said: "I'm a big fan of her game and mentality. Sometimes I think she's ice and I'm the fire.

"We needed to the find the balance. We did today."

The other semi-final will see Russians Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev face Czech pair Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik.

It was not all plain sailing for the leading singles players, with men's 24-time major winner Novak Djokovic and women's world number one Aryna Sabalenka suffering an early exit at the hands of Patten and Siniakova.

'The sort of semi-final line-up organisers envisaged'

Sabalenka and Djokovic lasted just 49 minutes, but this was otherwise a day where the singles stars edged out the doubles specialists.

With none of the four doubles pairs making it to the last four, the USTA has the sort of semi-final line up it envisaged when deciding to reinvent the mixed doubles 12 months ago.

Sabalenka and Djokovic turned out to be a very brief experiment. The other marquee pairing of Williams and Alcaraz lasted longer, with Williams in particular catching the eye in their first round win.

But with Alcaraz looking increasingly rusty in the quarter-final, Cobolli and Bencic won convincingly.

The Spaniard was wearing a compression sleeve on his right arm, and the skin fade of earlier in the year has been replaced by a mop of black hair.

This was useful court time for him, but did not really tell us anything about his chances of remaining in New York for the singles final in just under three weeks time.

articles.title: Serena Williams, Carlos Alcaraz 1st-Round Win Highlights US Open Mixed Doubles Day 1 Bracket Results
articles.summary: The mixed doubles tournament at the U.S. Open kicked off on Tuesday, with some big names—including Novak Djokovic, Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz—all in action.
articles.body:
The mixed doubles tournament at the U.S. Open kicked off on Tuesday, with some big names—including Novak Djokovic, Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz—all in action.

Here's a look at the day's results and best highlights.

Belinda Bencic/Flavio Cobolli def. Alexander Zverev/Taylor Townsend, 4-2, 4-2

Emma Navarro/Tommy Paul def. Amanda Anisimova/Learner Tien, 5(4)-3(1), 4-2

Katerina Siniakova/Henry Patten def. Aryna Sabalenka/Novak Djokovic, 1-4, 4-2, 1-1

Karlina Muchova/Jakub Mensik def. Kristina Mladenovic/Marcelo Arevalo, 4-1, 2-4, 1-0

Elina Svitolina/Gael Monfils def. Alexandra Eala/Felix Auger-Aliassime, 4-1, 4-1

Mirra Andreeva/Andrey Rublev def. Andrea Vavassori/Sara Errani, 1-4, 4-1, 1-0

Diana Shnaider/Casper Ruud def. Jessica Pegula/Taylor Fritz, 4-2, 4-1

Serena Williams/Carlos Alcaraz def. Erin Routliffe/Lloyd Glasspool, 5-3, 4-1

Karlina Muchova/Jakub Mensik def. Emma Navarro/Tommy Paul, 4-1, 4-3

Elina Svitolina/Gael Monfils def. Katerina Siniakova/Henry Patten 5-4, 4-5, 1-0

Belinda Bencic/Flavio Cobolli def. Serena Williams/Carlos Alcaraz, 5-4, 4-1

Mirra Andreeva/Andrey Rublev def. Diana Shnaider/Casper Ruud, 4-1, 4-5, 10-5

The duo of Vavassori and Errani falling in the first round was a major result, given they were the reigning U.S. Open mixed doubles champions.

It also wasn't a great day for the top seeds. The No. 1 seed, Sabalenka and Djokovic, fell in the first round. So did the No. 2 seed (Fritz and Pegula) and No. 3 seed (Anisimova and Tien).

The No. 4 seed Bencic and Cobolli is now the favorites, especially after eliminating the iconic duo of Williams and Alcaraz in the quarterfinals.

"I don't know how I landed on this court to play Carlos and Serena," Bencic said after the match. "It was an honor to play."

Alcaraz, meanwhile, certainly had some rust to shake off after being out of action since April.

"I think everybody could see: I double-faulted on the first point," he said. "I was really, really nervous. I was out for four months... I almost forget how it feels."

Bencic and Cobolli will now face Svitolina and Monfils in the semifinals, while the other match will pit Muchova and Mensik against Andreeva and Rublev.

articles.title: Haters of fashion attack Aryna Sabalenka with 'streetwalker' insult simply because she wore fishnet at US Open
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka's bold mesh dress at the US Open sparked fierce backlash, but the tennis star had a defiant response ready for her fashion critics.
articles.body: Good luck being a leader and trying something new, especially when it comes to fashion. I've said it before, I'm not an expert nor will I pretend to be one. That doesn’t mean there aren't others more than willing to pretend. There are, and they've set their sights on Aryna Sabalenka. She dared to show up to the US Open in what haters of fashion have labeled a fishnet dress. The adults out there may refer to it, correctly, as a mesh dress. I’d like to take a moment to thank Dua Lipa for several lessons in fashion, lessons that, let the record show, I retained despite being reluctantly dragged into them. NAOMI OSAKA'S ALL-BLACK FRENCH OPEN OUTFIT RIVALS HER JELLYFISH-INSPIRED LOOK FROM THE AUSTRALIAN OPEN It made it easier to spot what unfolded at Arthur Ashe Stadium. Sabalenka was on the court with her mixed doubles partner Novak Djokovic taking on Kateřina Siniaková and Henry Patten. She and Djokovic ended up losing the match. While dealing with the top-ranked in mixed doubles, the self-appointed fashion experts went on the attack. Who knew a little mesh would cause such a reaction? "How about that - Sabalenka leading the parade of streetwalker chic at the US Open with fishnet over shorts and a sports bra," one of the critics wrote. "Why does New York bring out all the trashy-ness?" SOCIAL MEDIA ERUPTS OVER NEW BROADCASTING GUIDELINES THAT DISCOURAGE 'SEXUALIZED' SHOTS OF FEMALE ATHLETES "Sabalenka ’s maximalist jewellery with those multicoloured stones set in gold clashes badly with her US open kit. Looks a mess imo," said another. One called it a "clown kit" and wrote in disbelief, "this sabalenka clown kit can’t be actually real." These attacks on her fashion didn’t catch Aryna Sabalenka by surprise. She knew they were coming. She was prepared for it after rolling out the new Nike looks a few weeks ago. "I love my outfit. If someone doesn't like it, it's okay. You cannot impress everyone with your outfits," she said earlier this month. "That's why I like fashion because there is room for whatever, basically." OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Take that, haters. Nice try. A mesh dress on top of shorts and a sports bra doesn't help you win your match. It also doesn't make you the leader of an imaginary "parade of streetwalker chic" either. I can't believe that had to be pointed out and that I had to be the one to do it. Yet here we are.

articles.title: Serena Williams Reacts to US Open Return in Video After Mixed Doubles with Carlos Alcaraz
articles.summary: Serena Williams returned to Arthur Ashe Stadium for the first time since 2022 to compete alongside Carlos Alcaraz in mixed doubles at the U.S. Open.
articles.body:
Serena Williams returned to Arthur Ashe Stadium for the first time since 2022 to compete alongside Carlos Alcaraz in mixed doubles at the U.S. Open.

She and Alcaraz started things off with a win over Erin Routliffe and Lloyd Glasspool, and the tennis legend was thrilled to be back on the court.

"I never expected to be back on this court, so it was just a really cool moment," Williams said. "I never thought this would happen."

Williams has been out of action for much of the last four years but got a bit of a warm-up this summer as she participated in various tournaments. Despite so much time off, she looked more than comfortable alongside Alcaraz.

Alcaraz has also been away for a significant amount of time, missing the last four months with a wrist injury. Playing alongside an all-time great was nerve-wracking, but ultimately helped him ease back into it.

"I was really nervous playing alongside Serena," Alcaraz said. "... She made it really easy for me just to try to enjoy it, go for it every time."

Following the win in the opening round, Williams and Alcaraz lost to Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli in the quarterfinals.

articles.title: Roger Federer Plays at US Open with John McEnroe, Andy Roddick, Agassi, Top Moments & Highlights
articles.summary: For one night, a legend was back on the court at Arthur Ashe Stadium for the first time since 2019.
articles.body:
For one night, a legend was back on the court at Arthur Ashe Stadium for the first time since 2019.

Roger Federer participated in a special exhibition event on Tuesday ahead of the start of the main draw at this year's U.S. Open. The 20-time Grand Slam champion was joined by Andy Roddick, John McEnroe and Andre Agassi for the celebratory matches.

Federer faced Roddick in a set of singles competition before teaming with McEnroe to go against Roddick and Agassi.

Agassi, Serena and more iconic US Open outfits

Perhaps the first hint at the magnitude of the night was the reaction Federer received before a coin toss that featured another notable name:

Once the tennis started, it was clear Federer hadn't lost his skills.

He cruised to a 6-3 victory over Roddick behind a powerful serve and some of his famous backhands:

It was an impressive showing considering how long he has been away from the game.

"I haven't played a singles set in, I don't know, (Hubert) Hurkacz at Wimbledon maybe, so it's been five years," Federer said Monday, per Brian Mahoney of the Associated Press. "I don't know how it's going to go tomorrow. So there is a lot of uncertainty but a lot of happiness that I can return to Arthur Ashe, a place where I have had so many beautiful moments."

The fans were happy to remember those beautiful moments Tuesday as they watched him play on the same court he enjoyed so much success on during the peak of his career.

Federer won five consecutive U.S. Open men's singles titles from 2004 through 2008. He also reached the final again in 2009 and 2015 and was a fan favorite for much of his run.

Those moments all came during his singles career, but he also mixed it up in the doubles match that was filled with notable names in the second half of Tuesday's performance.

He and McEnroe defeated Roddick and Agassi, 7-5, in a match that let all four of them show off their skills at various times.

While it was notable to see the 45-year-old back on the court, he also was quick to shut down any rumors about a potential comeback.

"No, no, no, no. No, not at all," Federer said ahead of the event. "Thanks for asking. I wasn't sure if the question was going to get asked, but I'm happy you did so I can clarify in case anybody thought."

Tuesday was just the start of what figures to be a celebratory week for the all-time great.

He is also the headliner of the 2026 International Tennis Hall of Fame class and will be enshrined Saturday in Newport, Rhode Island.
